preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 20 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for x in line.split()) and len(stdin.splitlines()) == m + 1 and (n := int(stdin.splitlines()[0].split()[0])) >= 1 and (m := int(stdin.splitlines()[0].split()[1])) >= 0 and m <= 400
preconditions.description: Input consists of exactly m+1 lines where the first line contains integers n (1 ≤ n ≤ 20) and m (0 ≤ m ≤ 400), followed by m lines each containing two integers vi and ui (1 ≤ vi, ui ≤ n) representing undirected edges. All values are within specified bounds.

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'Yes' if any(all(1 <= node <= n for node in path) and len(path) == n and all((path[i], path[i+1]) in {(u, v) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for u, v in [line.split()]} or (path[i+1], path[i]) in {(u, v) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for u, v in [line.split()]} for i in range(n-1)) for path in permutations(range(1, n+1))) else 'No'
postconditions.description: Output is 'Yes' if and only if there exists a Hamiltonian path (a path that visits each node exactly once) in the given undirected graph, otherwise 'No'. The path is determined by checking all permutations of nodes (1..n) and verifying if consecutive nodes in the permutation form an edge in the graph.
